text_en: Therefore those people were deservedly punished through such creatures, and were tormented by a multitude of animals.
text_cn: 因此，天主用同样的动物来惩罚他们，使他们受许多动物的残害，很为适当。

text_en: Instead of this punishment you showed kindness to your people, and you prepared quails to eat, a delicacy to satisfy the desire of appetite;
text_cn: 正与此惩罚相反，你却恩待了你的百姓，为满足他们的食欲；给他们预备了珍奇的美味——鹌鹑，当作食物。

text_en: in order that those people, when they desired food, might lose the least remnant of appetite because of the odious creatures sent to them, while your people, after suffering want a short time, might partake of delicacies.
text_cn: 那些想进食的埃及人，一看见上主遣来的丑陋的动物，连原有的食欲都失去了； 至于你的百姓，虽遭受了片时的饥饿，却分享了奇异的美味。

text_en: For it was necessary that upon those oppressors inescapable want should come, while to these others it was merely shown how their enemies were being tormented.
text_cn: 因为，埃及人残忍无道，理应遭受难挨的饥饿；至于你的百姓受饿，只是为叫他们明白，他们的仇敌受了如何的痛苦。

text_en: For when the terrible rage of wild animals came upon your people and they were being destroyed by the bites of writhing serpents, your wrath did not continue to the end;
text_cn: 以色列人固然也受到了猛兽的残害，和毒蛇的咬伤；

text_en: they were troubled for a little while as a warning, and received a symbol of deliverance to remind them of your law’s command.
text_cn: 但你的愤怒并没有坚持到底，只不过是为警戒他们，使他们暂时惊惶，获得救援的标记，好想起你的法令；

text_en: For the one who turned toward it was saved, not by the thing that was beheld, but by you, the Savior of all.
text_cn: 凡转向这标记的，并不是因着所瞻望的记号得救，而是因着你，万民的救主。

text_en: And by this also you convinced our enemies that it is you who deliver from every evil.
text_cn: 藉此，你向我们的仇敌证明：是你救人脱免一切灾祸；

text_en: For they were killed by the bites of locusts and flies, and no healing was found for them, because they deserved to be punished by such things.
text_cn: 因为蝗虫和苍蝇咬死了他们，却没有医治他们生命的方法，因为他们理应遭受这样的刑罚。

text_en: But your children were not conquered even by the fangs of venomous serpents, for your mercy came to their help and healed them.
text_cn: 但是你的子民，却没有为毒蛇的牙所制胜：这是因为你的仁慈前来救助，治好了他们。

text_en: To remind them of your oracles they were bitten, and then were quickly delivered, so that they would not fall into deep forgetfulness and become unresponsive to your kindness.
text_cn: 他们被咬后，即刻获治，是要他们记念你的话，免得他们深深遗忘，而不注意你的仁慈。

text_en: For neither herb nor poultice cured them, but it was your word, O Lord, that heals all people.
text_cn: 医好他们的，并不是草药，也不是膏药，上主，而是你那治好一切的话。

text_en: For you have power over life and death; you lead mortals down to the gates of Hades and back again.
text_cn: 因为，是你掌握生死的大权，引人下入阴府的门，而又领回。

text_en: A person in wickedness kills another, but cannot bring back the departed spirit, or set free the imprisoned soul.
text_cn: 人固然可以因邪恶而杀人，却不能使已离去的神魂再回来，也不能解救一个被囚在阴府中的灵魂。

text_en: To escape from your hand is impossible;
text_cn: 逃出你的掌握，那是不可能的。

text_en: for the ungodly, refusing to know you, were flogged by the strength of your arm, pursued by unusual rains and hail and relentless storms, and utterly consumed by fire.
text_cn: 为此，那不肯承认你的败类，遭受了你大力手臂的打击，受那罕有的大雨、冰雹与无情暴雨的袭击，并为火所毁灭。

text_en: For—most incredible of all—in water, which quenches all things, the fire had still greater effect, for the universe defends the righteous.
text_cn: 最堪惊奇的，是在能熄灭一切的水中，火焰反而更为炽（chì）烈，因为世界都为义人而战：

text_en: At one time the flame was restrained, so that it might not consume the creatures sent against the ungodly, but that seeing this they might know that they were being pursued by the judgment of God;
text_cn: 有时火势缓和，免得烧掉那些为对付不虔敬的人所派来的野兽，令他们见了，自知难逃天主正义的追击；

text_en: and at another time even in the midst of water it burned more intensely than fire, to destroy the crops of the unrighteous land.
text_cn: 有时火在水中反烧得异常炽烈，为烧尽毁灭不义之田的出产。

text_en: Instead of these things you gave your people food of angels, and without their toil you supplied them from heaven with bread ready to eat, providing every pleasure and suited to every taste.
text_cn: 相反地，你用天神之粮，养育了你的子民；他们不必操劳，你从天上给他们降下了现成的食粮，具有各种美味，适合各人的口味。

text_en: For your sustenance manifested your sweetness toward your children; and the bread, ministering to the desire of the one who took it, was changed to suit everyone’s liking.
text_cn: 你赐予的食粮，合乎取食者的嗜好，随着人的愿望而变化，这表明你对待儿女如何恩爱。

text_en: Snow and ice withstood fire without melting, so that they might know that the crops of their enemies were being destroyed by the fire that blazed in the hail and flashed in the showers of rain;
text_cn: 雪和冰遇着火并不融化， 这是使他们知道：为毁灭仇敌的收获，火曾在冰雹中炽燃，在雨水中闪烁；

text_en: whereas the fire, in order that the righteous might be fed, even forgot its native power.
text_cn: 但为养育义人，火却忘记了自己的本能。

text_en: For creation, serving you who made it, exerts itself to punish the unrighteous, and in kindness relaxes on behalf of those who trust in you.
text_cn: 实在，受造物都服从你，自己的造主，致力惩罚不义的人，恩待信赖你的人。

text_en: Therefore at that time also, changed into all forms, it served your all-nourishing bounty, according to the desire of those who had need,
text_cn: 因此，“玛纳”就依照你那养育众人的恩宠，起种种变化，来适应需求者的愿望，

text_en: so that your children, whom you loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the production of crops that feeds humankind but that your word sustains those who trust in you.
text_cn: 为使你所爱的子女们知道：上主，养育世人的，不是各种果食，而是你的言语，保全了信赖你的人。

text_en: For what was not destroyed by fire was melted when simply warmed by a fleeting ray of the sun,
text_cn: 因为，火所不能烧毁的，因着温和的一线阳光，立即融化，

text_en: to make it known that one must rise before the sun to give you thanks, and must pray to you at the dawning of the light;
text_cn: 使人知道：在太阳没有升起以前，就应赞颂你；在曙光破晓时分，就该祈求你；

text_en: for the hope of an ungrateful person will melt like wintry frost, and flow away like waste water.
text_cn: 因为，不知恩者的希望，就如冬天的霜，势必消溶，逝去有如无用的流水。
